code_written_limitations: Unallocated complaints (computed by code from `area_rollup.json`): 20.0% (A16) of complaint and cancellation records (6 (A10)) are general/unspecified: generic criticism (for example "worst update") that names no specific area, so they are not allocated to any of the four decision areas. If many of them refer to one area's problem, for example the same free-tier change, that area's total is understated; the labels cannot show which area that would be.

Premium-only boundary, upper-bound sensitivity (computed by code; `analysis/premium_only_sensitivity.json`): 2 (T55) of the 8 (C01) `billing.premium_only` complaint and cancellation records contain no Premium or payment word (premium, subscri-, pay/paid/paying, free, buy, money, trial, $; case-insensitive), with a severity sum of 6 (T56). If none of them belonged to billing/support, its severity sum would fall from 29 (A02) to 23 (T57), still above every other decision area (usability 17 (A05), playback/performance 13 (A08) and access/onboarding 0 (T58)). This is an upper bound, not a relabelling: many of these reviews plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle), and they were not moved to any other area.
mandatory_limitations: Counts describe the labeled reviews in a 60-review development checkpoint (input.csv), not the full corpus: self-selected public app reviews, not a customer population. They carry no revenue, plan tier or confirmed cancellations, so revenue at risk cannot be computed.
Cancellation language is expressed intent, not observed churn; nothing here estimates a causal effect on retention.
Star ratings and helpful votes were not used to classify; severity is judged from the text under the shared rubric.
4 completed records are flagged needs_review, 0 are quarantined and 0 are unfinished.

Golden set (evals/golden/results.json): on 50 human-labelled reviews the pipeline's labels match the human labels on topic 78%, intent 76% and severity 74% (exact); 50 cases are a diagnostic of label quality, not a precise accuracy estimate.

alternatives.why_not_first: Usability's severity sum {A05} across {A04} complaint and cancellation reviews trails billing/support's {A02}, and its share of reviews grew less ({T15} versus billing/support's {T09}) between {T01} and {T02}; however, the verifier's own labels rank usability first by severity sum ({T46}), which is the main reason to flag it as a close alternative.

Playback/performance has the lowest severity sum ({A08} across {A07} complaint and cancellation reviews) of the three decision areas with a clear ranking, and its share of reviews barely moved between {T01} and {T02} ({T12}), showing little growth pressure relative to billing/support.

No top issues or complaint/severity figures are reported for this area in the aggregate table (its severity sum under the premium-only sensitivity check is {T58}), so there is no evidence here to support prioritizing it over billing/support.

limitations: The verifier's disagreement on the top area (usability by its labels versus billing/support by the enricher's labels) is based on a small sample of {T42} reviews, so it cannot settle which area truly leads in severity.

The premium_only issue mixes free-tier packaging complaints with a few records lacking a clear Premium or payment word; the true boundary of this issue is uncertain beyond the sensitivity check already reported.

Spike-month figures for billing.premium_only ({T30}) are drawn from a single month ({T25}) with few full-month reviews ({T26} against a median of {T27}), so they cannot confirm whether the issue is a sustained pattern.

The data cannot show whether addressing free-tier packaging would change expressed cancellation intent into retained usage, since these are self-selected reviews rather than a tracked customer cohort.
next_quarter_actions: Review and test changes to free-tier shuffle, skip-limit and rewind restrictions tied to billing.premium_only ({C01} complaint reviews, severity sum {C02}); watch for the issue's complaint count and severity sum, and its share of complaints ({T16}), to fall if packaging changes land well.

Investigate the charged-without-account-access flow behind billing.payment ({C21} review, severity sum {C22}, mean severity {C23}) to clarify account linkage at the point of charge; watch for its severity sum to fall.
As a hedge on the closest alternative, test ad-frequency/pacing changes for usability.ads ({C09} complaint reviews, severity sum {C10}) and watch for its complaint count and severity sum to fall.
rationale: Billing/support leads on baseline priority with severity sum {A02} across {A01} complaint and cancellation reviews, ahead of usability's severity sum {A05} and playback/performance's severity sum {A08}; within billing/support the premium_only issue (severity sum {C02} across {C01} reviews) and the payment-access issue (severity sum {C22}) are the top drivers.

Trend: billing/support's share of reviews rose from {T07} in {T01} to {T08} in {T02}, a change of {T09}, the largest increase among the four decision areas (usability moved {T15}, playback/performance moved {T12}); this growth supports, but does not by itself establish, the recommendation.

Billing/support's share of complaints is {T16} (interval {T17} to {T18}), which overlaps with usability's share {T19} (interval {T20} to {T21}) and playback/performance's share {T22} (interval {T23} to {T24}), so the complaint-share lead is within sampling error, even though the severity-sum lead is not undermined by this.

Robustness caveat: the independent verifier, scoring the same sample of {T42} reviews, ranks usability on top by its own severity sum ({T46} versus billing/support's {T43} under enricher labels, or {T48} under verifier labels) - a labelling disagreement that makes this recommendation provisional, not a sampling artifact to dismiss.

Upper-bound sensitivity: even if the {T55} premium_only records without a Premium or payment word are excluded, billing/support's severity sum would be {T57}, still above usability's {A05} and playback/performance's {A08}, so the lead is not solely an artifact of those borderline records.
output.recommendation: Billing/support carries the highest baseline priority among the four decision areas, driven chiefly by the free tier playback restrictions issue (billing.premium_only), with {C01} complaint and cancellation reviews and severity sum {C02} (mean severity {C03}), plus the charged-without-account-access issue (billing.payment, {C21} review, severity sum {C22}, mean severity {C23}). The premium_only issue is free-tier packaging and entitlement policy work - what the free tier includes and how changes to it (skip limits, forced shuffle, no repeat or rewind) are rolled out and explained - not a payment or checkout defect, so the next quarter's work should be a product/policy review of free-tier packaging plus a smaller fix for the account-access-at-charge issue.
what_would_change_the_call: If a human audit of the {T55} premium_only records without a Premium or payment word found that many are not about free-tier restrictions, that would weaken (not strengthen) the case for billing/support's severity sum.

If billing/support's share of reviews reverses back toward its {T07} level in the same months of the following year rather than holding near {T08}, that would weaken the trend support for this recommendation.
If the verifier's severity-sum ordering (favoring usability) held on a larger verified sample beyond the current {T42} reviews, that would favor usability over billing/support.

payload.question: Where should the next quarter of product-improvement effort go: access/onboarding, usability, playback/performance, or billing/support?

top_issues.summary: Free users are frustrated that forced shuffle, skip limits, and inability to pick or rewind songs now require a Premium subscription.

top_issues.definition: Too many, too long, too loud or repeated ads; ads interrupting listening.
top_issues.name: Excessive ad frequency

top_issues.definition: Recommendations, the algorithm, autoplay or radio picks, the DJ, unwanted suggested songs.

top_issues.definition: App crashes, freezes, will not open or load, blank screens.
top_issues.name: App freezing and failing to play music
top_issues.summary: Customers report the app freezes when selecting a channel, preventing music playback and disrupting their listening experience.

top_issues.definition: Notifications, emails, settings, toggles, widgets and other interaction annoyances.
top_issues.name: Other control annoyances

top_issues.definition: Lyrics missing, wrong or not loading.
top_issues.name: Lyrics feature unavailable
top_issues.summary: Customers report that the lyrics feature is missing from the app, preventing them from viewing song lyrics while listening.

top_issues.definition: Lag, slowness, battery or storage use, audio quality or volume problems.

top_issues.summary: Customers report that premium streaming audio quality is poor and falls short of competitors, diminishing their listening experience.

period_comparison.comparison_scope: areas lists the four decision areas only; areas that are not decision options are under non_decision_areas
period_comparison.method: share = complaint/cancellation reviews in the area / all classified reviews in the period; Wilson 95% intervals; identical calendar months one year apart avoid the partial first/last months and seasonal mix. Descriptive only: reviews are self-selected, not a customer census.

premium_only_sensitivity.interpretation: Upper-bound sensitivity, not a relabelling. It assumes that none of the records without a Premium or payment word belongs in billing/support and adds them to no other area. Many of them plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle, no repeat or rewind), and non-English payment words (for example 'paisa') are not matched, so the real effect is smaller than shown.
premium_only_sensitivity.what: upper-bound sensitivity of the billing/support lead to the premium-only topic boundary, computed by code; not a relabelling
